title: Cross-project silent-loss, output-finalization, and OBJECTS-root acceptance
mode: Primary-source web research with local plan and focused-test receipt crosswalk
scope: Refresh LibreDWG's current published AcDs/SAB implementation boundary and the independently reported 3D carrier-loss, truncated-output, and NOD-order failure shapes.
Map the reports to existing PAR-07/S8, strict conversion finalization, and PAR-20/7G.3 owners without creating duplicate findings or tests.
Refine the implementation sequence around fast generated selectors, route-specific strict checks, and one later composed external/native checkpoint.

sources.revision: Public current NEWS page accessed 2026-10-20; cited claims are in the v0.14 release notes.
sources.observed: The release notes say the AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b DataStorage parser is not fully implemented, R2013+ SAB extraction is still performed by brute force, and SAB v2 to encrypted SAT v1 conversion is a separate compatibility step needed for pre-R2013 DXF.
sources.limits: Release-note statements describe LibreDWG's named implementation and version context. They are not a normative format specification, a libdxfrw defect report, or independent topology validation.

sources.revision: Public issue page accessed 2026-10-20; report identifies LibreDWG 0.14.8593 at commit 8a1ae764.
sources.observed: The issue body gives a from-scratch AC1032 DXF recipe for a REGION carrying a cube-derived SAB payload, reports 5,489 expected bytes, and describes the named LibreDWG DXF-to-DWG-to-DXF route preserving the REGION shell while losing the SAB/ACDSDATA. It also describes an unavailable confidential customer DWG, which was not retrieved.
sources.limits: The scratch recipe can probe DXF carrier handling but the reported LibreDWG-generated DWG is not a positive AcDs fixture. The report does not establish current master behavior, libdxfrw behavior, or independent B-rep semantics.

sources.revision: Public issue page accessed 2026-10-20; issue reports an AC1032 case and compares output with ODA File Converter 25.6.
sources.observed: The report describes a truncated DXF without complete sections or EOF while the command returns status 0, despite a nonzero LINE inventory from another route.
sources.limits: This is a peer-specific reported failure shape, not a local reproduction. The attached drawing was not downloaded.

sources.revision: Public issue page accessed 2026-10-20; report states it is present on LibreDWG v0.14 and master as of 2026-09-08.
sources.observed: The issue reports that choosing the lowest-handle DICTIONARY can place an extension-owned dictionary before the NOD, causing readers to select the wrong root and lose layout names. The author reports a root-first reorder changing only two of 43 production drawings, preserving OBJECTS content, and satisfying the first-unowned-DICTIONARY rule on 141 shipped DWGs.
sources.limits: Corpus counts and application comparisons are reporter evidence, not locally reproduced results. Root identity is distinct from ordering every ownership edge and from dictionary key order.

sources.project: Autodesk and ezdxf OBJECTS ordering contracts
sources.revision: Autodesk DXF reference and ezdxf stable OBJECTS documentation accessed 2026-10-20.
sources.observed: Autodesk says the NOD is always the first OBJECTS object; ezdxf describes hierarchical owner order starting with the NOD as the first OBJECTS object.
sources.limits: These contracts establish the root-first and owner-order requirements but do not imply that non-owning references should be topologically scheduled.

sources.project: Local plan and focused implementation receipts
sources.revision: Plan and route-specific test receipts inspected 2026-10-20.
sources.observed: The generated PlotSettings and VisualStyle controls assert NOD-first plus owner-dictionary-before-child physical order for their respective ASCII/Binary routes. Their focused CTests and scoped builds are recorded as passing in their implementation receipts. Existing plan owners already cover strict EOF/transactional output and modeler carrier disposition.
sources.limits: The two graph controls do not establish a generic OBJECTS scheduler, every object family, external producer behavior, application acceptance, or 3D semantics. The new research pass did not rerun them or the full suite.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-07/S8: record exact ACIS carrier bytes/chunks, schema and entity association separately from B-rep semantics; distinguish generated DXF carrier probes from qualified DWG producers.
Strict conversion/finalization owner: independently require command success, closed sections/final marker, strict reparse, source-object disposition accounting, and no partial publication.
PAR-20/7G.3: for admitted graph routes assert true NOD identity/first position, then owner-before-owned order, then key/handle/owner/target closure; do not infer root from numeric handle.
Validation cadence: use generated focused selectors and their owning fast CTests per slice; reserve exact-pinned peer/native checks for the existing composed checkpoint.
assessment.referencedFocusedTests: PASS: libdxfrw_plotsettings_visualstyle_shade_reference (1/1) and libdxfrw_extension_graph_limits (1/1), rerun during final validation.

planChanges: Added a newest plan summary connecting LibreDWG's documented AcDs/SAB limitations to the existing carrier, finalization, and OBJECTS graph owners.
Added a detailed source crosswalk for LibreDWG #1411, #1355, and #1413, keeping each report explicitly peer-scoped and non-promoting.
Clarified that the #1411 scratch recipe is suitable for a DXF carrier probe only; it is not a positive DWG AcDs producer or a B-rep oracle.
Made output completion an explicit conjunction of process status, section/EOF closure, strict parse, source-object accounting, and atomic publication, while reusing existing local test owners.
Connected the newly passing PlotSettings and VisualStyle generated order controls to NOD identity-first and owner-before-owned gates without claiming a generic scheduler.
limitations: Public peer issue bodies and release notes were reviewed; peer reports were not reproduced.
No customer drawing or issue attachment was downloaded.
No peer executable, native CAD application, or geometry kernel was run.
The six external-only J items remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and cannot be promoted by this research.
